update: Resume where you left off across devices
notes: Shares the PlaybackState spec with the F4 shuffle cycle; /replica-architect specifies it before build.

F5 model (one, chosen): a download is a copy of the user's own file on that device; it plays offline with no periodic online check-in while the file stays in the library and the account exists, including after a downgrade or a cancelled paid plan (the F7 over-quota rule). It is removed when the user removes the download or signs out of that device; when the file leaves the library (the user deletes it, or the F7 over-quota policy deletes it after notice); when access to it is disabled after a valid copyright notice (fixes.md section 7); and when the library is deleted under F7 (account deletion, termination under the terms, the inactivity rule or a shutdown). With no check-in, the device removes its copy at its next connection, so a device that stays offline keeps playing it until then; whether takedowns need a bounded check-in is an open question for /replica-architect and counsel. Single track, album, playlist or whole library. Available on every plan; the plan sets the number of download devices (caps front-loaded egress). After a downgrade or cancel above the new device cap, the user picks which devices keep downloads (default most recently used); the others remove their copies at next connection, after notice, within the F7 N-day window. If /replica-launch makes offline paid, switch fully to a lapse-after-grace model and drop keeps-playing wording. Parity for owners (the original's Local Files, YouTube Music uploads, Plexamp), so a feature line not a pitch; built after the waitlist gate. The store billing route (fixes.md section 7, chosen in /replica-launch) covers every paid plan, including extra download devices. Replaces the note calling it the key paid feature.
F5: keep downloads in app storage that the OS does not treat as purgeable cache (check current iOS and Android docs); show space used per device and the device count against the plan cap.

notes: F7 over-quota rule, the one rule for downgrade and cancel (cancelling a paid plan moves the user to the free tier): a library within the new quota stays as it is; over it, uploads pause at once; playback, downloads and export continue for N days; then the user chooses what to keep within quota and the rest is deleted after notice. Replaces the recon F09 edge read-only until under (recon F09 now carries this rule). N is set in /replica-launch and reviewed by counsel. The free quota is the main pricing decision: /replica-launch sets it as a number (GB or tracks) from the cost model and records the monthly cost of one free user, an assumed free-to-paid ratio and the free-tier cost carried by each paying user; it is a trial size, not a rival to the free lockers. Free accounts also fall under the F7 inactivity rule (notice by email, deletion after a stated period with no sign-in, export open throughout).

F7: cancelling a paid plan moves the user to the free tier and the over-quota rule on Storage quota per plan with usage meter applies (a library within the free quota stays; over it, uploads pause, playback, downloads and export continue for N days, the user picks what to keep within the free quota, and the rest is deleted after notice). The whole library is deleted only when the user deletes the account (an export offered first), when the account is terminated under the terms (including the repeat-infringer policy), when a free account falls under the inactivity rule, or when the service shuts down after notice.
